chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from a group of his narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, who said:

I asked Aba Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), 'May I be your sacrifice! What is the reward for one who visits the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) with the intention of visiting?' He replied, 'Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith from Imam al-Jawad (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual merit of visiting the Prophet’s grave with deliberate intention (*mu'tamidan*). It underscores the Shia tradition of *Ziyarat* not merely as a physical act but as a means of drawing closer to the Prophet, with the ultimate reward being Paradise, reflecting the high status of the Ahl al-Bayt's guidance in interceding for believers.
